gaps.construct: raise JSONDecodeError("Extra data", s, end) - an exception carrying a message, the document and a position
gaps.description: The doc only shows failures as bare names (`fail with OutOfRange`); there is no way to attach data to a failure. Invented `fail with JSONDecodeError with msg ... and doc ... and pos ...`.

gaps.construct: Result of any Python type (dict/list/str/int/float/bool/None, or whatever object_hook returns)
gaps.description: No dynamic or open 'any' type; a closed JsonValue choice was declared, which cannot represent object_hook/parse_float custom results.

gaps.construct: _w=WHITESPACE.match default parameter, and keyword argument idx=
gaps.description: No default or keyword arguments and no function values; the parameter is dropped and the helper called directly, so callers overriding _w cannot be expressed.
No methods; self becomes an explicit `with decoder` parameter.

gaps.construct: Tuple return and unpacking: obj, end = self.raw_decode(...)
gaps.description: No tuples or multiple results; a single-use record type DecodeResult is declared and fields read with `of`.

gaps.construct: len(s) on a str, and regex match of whitespace
gaps.description: The doc shows `count of` only for lists and `length` only in a refinement; it is unclear which gives the length of Text. Regex matching has no vocabulary, so it is hidden behind a declared helper.

invented_syntax: fail with JSONDecodeError with msg "Extra data" and doc s and pos end
notes: Simple control flow translates cleanly and the `fails with` header is a real improvement over Python's invisible raise. The two blockers are failures that carry data (almost every real exception does) and the absence of a dynamic/any type for decoders that return host-language objects.
